newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn says 97 deficit may be well over 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn says 97 deficit may be well over 3 pct.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday that France's public deficit could be "significantly higher" than the 3.0 percent forecast in the 1997 finance act.
He noted that parliamentarian Philippe Auberger had said the deficit this year would be 3.4 percent of gross domestic product.

"One can fear it will be more. One can hope he is right," he told a news conference. "If Auberger is right -- and I hope the deficit is 3.4 percent - it will be easy. If the audit says it is 3.8 percent the situation is a bit different".
The government is awaiting the results of an audit of public finances due on July 21.
